scope: Approved Codex cuts and minimal kernel builder protocol relocation/reference repair

removed_rules.previous_text: [CX-000] NAME: Handshake Codex.
[CX-002] PURPOSE: Shared repo authority, used with the build-rules registry and the assigned role protocol.
[CX-100] Preserve Raw / Derived / Display separation: canonical changes belong in Raw; recompute derived data and display projections rather than treating them as authority.
[CX-101] Route model calls through Handshake's shared model client/adapters; feature modules must not embed provider-specific invocation paths.
[CX-103] Route database and filesystem operations through the canonical storage/resource boundaries with authenticated identity and resource authorization.
[CX-104] Use shared production logging and observability rather than ad hoc output; diagnostic access must preserve the protected resource's visibility.

[CX-132] Preserve account-bound resource ownership, default-deny access, same-project privacy, non-widening derivatives, actor attribution, revocation and immutable session context across local and remote boundaries. HBR-PRIV and the Master Spec own the detailed obligations.

[CX-032] Verify claims against current authority, source, runtime or external evidence before acting. Memory, chat summaries and plausible reconstruction are not facts; label unavailable verification UNVERIFIED or NOT_INSPECTED. Explicitly requested brainstorming remains non-authoritative.

[CX-032C] On correction, stop defending, inspect the relevant evidence and correct the affected claim before further mutation. Explanation-only requests permit read-only fact gathering, not unrequested repairs.

[CX-972] Deliver the requested outcome first. Do supporting work only when it directly enables that outcome or records its result; do not substitute paperwork, adjacent improvements or proxy evidence for completion.

[CX-971] The Operator owns scope and stopping. Preserve every requested requirement, obey explicit stops immediately, and do not use token/session capacity as a reason to drop or defer work. Work evidenced dependencies within authorization; report an exact external blocker when no permitted action can resolve it.
[CX-653A] Consolidation must preserve original intent, constraints, unresolved work and status unless the Operator explicitly retires or replaces them.

[CX-PROOF-004] Record failures, missing proof and dependencies honestly. Do not weaken acceptance, fabricate signatures, invent evidence, or call a blocker removed until the requested outcome is independently verified at its canonical boundary.

[CX-503I1] Use focused proof while iterating and the required broad proof at the declared batch/final boundary. Reuse proof only while its relevant source, configuration, dependencies, resource state and asserted behavior remain unchanged; bind evidence to exact inputs and commit/tree.

[CX-573F] Prove claimed behavior at the executable runtime or named real Handshake-managed resource boundary. Compilation, declarations, generated schemas, mocks and fixture-only tests cannot substitute for required runtime, persistence, privacy, replay or GUI proof.

[CX-PROOF-001] Inspect the actual artifact against its reference before judging it. For GUI work, follow HBR's Argus inspection and steering requirements; green tests or an unopened screenshot are not visual verification.

[CX-PROOF-003] Delegate only within assigned authority and disjoint ownership. The parent remains responsible for reviewing delegated changes, proof and cleanup; sub-agents gain no additional role, worktree, merge or process authority.
[CX-984-004] Proof binaries must come from the owner's own worktree and scoped build; an unrelated shared-target binary proves nothing about the current source.
[CX-984-005] Database proof uses an isolated WP-scoped SurrealDB namespace/database, never shared divergent authority state.
[CX-984-007] Build residue must not contain governance artifacts or governance runtime state; preserve those in their separate `.GOV/` and external governance-runtime locations.

[CX-105C] Master Spec edits retain copy-first versioned bundles: preserve the previous bundle and update the new bundle's uniform version, manifest, resolver, hashes, changelog and SPEC_CURRENT together.
[CX-106] New top-level directories require explicit Operator approval.
